title: Planck and the Cosmic Microwave Background
notes: Read live via curl with a browser user-agent. Supports: the hot Big Bang state with extremely high density and temperature, the universe expanding ever since (observations since the late 1920s); recombination about 380,000 years after the Big Bang at about 3000 K when electrons combined with protons to form hydrogen atoms and the universe became transparent; CMB photons redshifted by expansion to about 1 mm wavelength and 2.7 K (roughly -270 C); CMB predicted in the late 1940s by Gamow, Alpher, and Herman; detected accidentally by Penzias and Wilson (ESA dates the first detection 1964), Nobel Prize in Physics 1978; COBE (1989) measured a blackbody spectrum at 2.73 K with fluctuations of about 1 part in 100,000 (2006 Nobel to Mather and Smoot); WMAP launched 2001; Planck launched 2009; the CMB's tiny fluctuations grew under gravity into galaxies, clusters, and the large-scale structure. Used for original synthesis only.
